---
title: Testing reference
description: How tests are defined and run in Oxygen
type: reference
---

Tests live in their own `.test.yml` files. Each file points at one agent
(its **target**), lists a set of **cases** — a prompt plus the answer you
expect — and says how many times to run each one. An LLM judge scores every
run against the expected answer.

<Note>
Only `.agentic.yml` agents can be tested. Inline `tests:` blocks in
`.agent.yml` or `.workflow.yml` files are no longer supported — `.test.yml` is
the only way to define tests.
</Note>

## Test file format

```yaml sales.agentic.test.yml
target: sales.agentic.yml   # optional — inferred from the filename

settings:
  concurrency: 5            # runs executed in parallel
  runs: 3                   # times to run each case
  judge_model: gpt-5-mini   # model that scores each run

cases:
  - name: signups-last-month
    prompt: "How many users signed up last month?"
    expected: "1,247 new user signups"
    tags: [users, critical]

  - prompt: "Show me top 5 customers by lifetime value"
    expected: |
      A ranked list of 5 customers ordered by total spend,
      including customer names and their LTV amounts.
    tags: [customers]
```

### Top-level fields

| Field      | Type   | Default                | Description |
| ---------- | ------ | ---------------------- | ----------- |
| `target`   | string | inferred from filename | Path to the `.agentic.yml` agent under test. If omitted, `sales.agentic.test.yml` targets `sales.agentic.yml` in the same directory. |
| `name`     | string | —                      | Optional display name for the test file. |
| `settings` | object | see below              | Run settings. |
| `cases`    | list   | required               | The test cases. |

### `settings`

| Field         | Type    | Default | Description |
| ------------- | ------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `runs`        | integer | `3`     | Number of times each case is run. Consistency is measured as agreement across these runs. |
| `concurrency` | integer | `5`     | How many runs execute in parallel. |
| `judge_model` | string  | —       | Model used as the LLM judge. Prefer a different model family than the agent's to avoid self-preference bias. |

### `cases`

| Field      | Type            | Default  | Description |
| ---------- | --------------- | -------- | ----------- |
| `prompt`   | string          | required | The question sent to the agent. |
| `expected` | string          | required | The expected answer. The judge checks each run's answer for factual consistency with it. |
| `name`     | string          | —        | Stable label for the case, used by `--case` and shown in progress output instead of the prompt. |
| `tags`     | list of strings | `[]`     | Tags for filtering with `--tag`. |
| `tool`     | string          | —        | Accepted by the schema, but tool-use assertions are not enforced yet — setting it has no effect on pass/fail. |

## How evaluation works

For each case, Oxygen:

1. Runs the target agent `runs` times with the case's `prompt`
2. Asks the judge model whether each answer is factually consistent with
   `expected` — formatting and wording differences are ignored
3. Records a pass rate per case, and whether all runs reached the same verdict

Across the file, the **score** is the overall pass rate over every case and
run, and **consistency** is the fraction of cases whose runs all agreed.

## Running tests

Run tests from the **Tests** page in the Oxygen IDE, which lists every test
file in the project along with past runs, or from the CLI:

```sh
# Run every .test.yml file in the project
oxy test

# Run one file
oxy test sales.agentic.test.yml

# Only cases tagged "critical"
oxy test --tag critical

# One case, by 0-based index, name, or exact prompt
oxy test sales.agentic.test.yml --case signups-last-month
```

### Accuracy thresholds

Use `--min-accuracy` to fail the command (exit code 1) when the score is below
a threshold — useful as a CI quality gate:

```sh
oxy test --min-accuracy 0.8
```

Each test file produces one score. When several files run,
`--threshold-mode` controls how the threshold is applied: `average` (default)
checks the average score across files; `all` requires every file's score to
meet it.

```sh
oxy test --min-accuracy 0.8 --threshold-mode all
```

### Machine-readable output

`--format json` prints the full results as JSON on stdout. `--output-json`
also writes the JSON to a file next to the test file
(`sales.agentic.test.results.json`, or `test-results.json` when running every
file).

```sh
oxy test sales.agentic.test.yml --format json --quiet
```

## CLI reference

```sh
oxy test [FILE] [OPTIONS]
```

- `FILE` — path to a `.test.yml` file. Omit it to run every `.test.yml` file in
  the project.

| Flag                         | Short | Description | Default |
| ---------------------------- | ----- | ----------- | ------- |
| `--tag <tag>`                |       | Only run cases with this tag | — |
| `--case <case>`              |       | Only run one case, by 0-based index, `name`, or exact prompt. Requires `FILE` | — |
| `--format <format>`          |       | Output format: `pretty` or `json` | `pretty` |
| `--output-json`              |       | Also write full JSON results to a file | `false` |
| `--min-accuracy <threshold>` |       | Minimum score (0.0–1.0). Exit code 1 if below | — |
| `--threshold-mode <mode>`    |       | `average` or `all` | `average` |
| `--quiet`                    | `-q`  | Show only the results summary | `false` |
| `--verbose`                  | `-v`  | Show agent steps, actual output, and judge reasoning | `false` |

## CI example

```yaml
- name: Run agent tests
  run: oxy test --min-accuracy 0.8 --quiet
```

## Error handling

- **Wrong file type** — `oxy test` rejects any file that doesn't end in
  `.test.yml`, and any test whose target isn't an `.agentic.yml` agent.
- **No tests found** — running `oxy test` with no file fails if the project has
  no `.test.yml` files.
- **Threshold failures** — the command exits with code 1 only when
  `--min-accuracy` is set and not met. If no score was produced, it prints a
  warning and exits 0.
